title: Signal harvest diary and microfeature claims — May 2026
body:
Snapshot / purpose:
Quick harvest of field signals from Apr–May 2026 calls, support tickets, and AMAs. Aim: turn fragmented asks into a small set of testable microfeatures we can prototype in a sprint or pair with product experiments. This is intentionally lightweight — think: 1-pager plus ticket sketches not a full PRD.

What this contains (fast index):
- Headline themes (3) with confidence levels
- 9 microfeature claims (short hypothesis, rough impact, quick owner)
- Representative verbatim customer blurbs (for empathy)
- Suggested probes + measurement for a 2-week experiment
- Open questions and next steps (who to pester)

Notes on sources and bias:
- Data sources: 28 support threads (CS bucket), 7 post-demo survey forms, 3 sales discovery calls, and slack log of a beta customer pilot.
- Bias: heavier on mid-market SaaS customers (two large accounts) and skew toward inference-cost concerns. Low sampling of air-gapped/on-prem customers this round.

Headline themes (short)
1) Cost friction at token scale (HIGH confidence) — customers want clearer levers for cost vs. quality; they often ask for specific knobs rather than general advice.
2) Fallback transparency (MEDIUM confidence) — developers see unexpected model fallbacks and can’t trace why a cheaper model was chosen. Leads to trust issues in production.
3) SDK ergonomics for batch embedding pipelines (MEDIUM-HIGH confidence) — repeated customer notes about brittle backoff/retry behavior, missing explicit batching helpers in SDKs.

Microfeature claims (actionable, ranked by simplicity)
(1) cost-savings preview toggle (low effort)
- Claim: adding a client-side preview that shows estimated token cost/time for a request given current routing/batching policies will reduce tagging of 'unexpected cost' tickets by ~30%.
- Why: customers repeatedly asked for a \"what will this cost\" before sending high-volume jobs.
- Quick probe: add a flag in SDK that calls existing cost-estimator endpoint and surfaces an estimate. Track support ticket incidence and feature usage.
- Owner: SDK + product; ticket stub: CS-claim-cost-preview

(2) explicit-fallback audit log (medium effort)
- Claim: adding per-request metadata in Console/Logs that shows which fallback rule (region, model-variant, tier) was applied will cut time-to-root-cause for downgrade incidents by ~40%.
- Why: multiple reports of \"model swapped for cheaper one; app got worse\" without traceable reason.
- Probe: surface a simple column in request logs for 2 weeks for a set of customers and collect feedback.
- Owner: Observability + infra; ticket stub: CS-claim-fallback-audit

(3) batching helper utilities in SDK (low effort)
- Claim: provide a small set of batching helpers (auto-chunk, retry with exponential backoff tuned for our runtime) will reduce customer integration time by ~25% and reduce retry storms.
- Probe: release alpha helpers in JS SDK and onboard two customers; measure integration time and number of post-release support threads.

(4) model-variant explainability endpoint (higher effort)
- Claim: a read-call that returns a human-readable explanation of model variant differences (cost, expected latency, quality notes) reduces friction during rollout and model pinning.
- Probe: mocked endpoint (static mapping) for top 6 variants for 3 weeks; survey users.

(5) dev-mode dryrun for heavy-embedding jobs (low-medium effort)
- Claim: a dry-run that samples 1% of inputs and returns projected total cost + distributions helps teams budget and prevents overconsumption incidents.
- Probe: CLI flag + small UI affordance in Console; track adoption.

(6) per-route token anomaly alerts (medium effort)
- Claim: automated alerts when token consumption per request changes > 3x baseline will catch broken prompts or bad caching regressions earlier.
- Probe: pilot with three accounts that volunteered. Collect false-positive rate.

(7) guided quantization advice for workloads (research + product; higher effort)
- Claim: a lightweight recommender that suggests quantization profiles by sampling 100 requests and running a quick eval will reduce avg serving cost by X% while staying within user-defined quality thresholds.
- Probe: internal lab run then pilot.

(8) SDK-level request tagging and trace passthrough (low effort)
- Claim: allow customers to pass their own trace-id/application-tag through requests for easier correlation in their tracing systems; expected high ROI for debug speed.
- Probe: expose passthrough header and include in Console UI search.

(9) humanized retry messaging (UX tweak; very low effort)
- Claim: change default retry error messages in SDK from opaque codes to actionable text (\"attempting cheaper model due to capacity; pin model if you need consistent behavior\") to reduce support question load.
- Probe: roll change in one minor release; watch support volume.

Representative customer quotes (verbatim snippets)
- \"We ran a job and watched costs spike overnight — wish I had a preview. Felt like a blind auction.\" — mid-market analytics platform
- \"Why did the model change? The logs show a different model id but not why. We had to rollback.\" — fintech PM
- \"Our embedding pipeline keeps falling over when we hit bursts; SDK helpers would save us a week of engineering.\" — search startup eng lead

Quick measurement ideas (what \"success\" looks like)
- For cost-preview: reduce \"unexpected cost\" tickets by 30% within 8 weeks; adoption > 20% of heavy-job users.
- For fallback audit log: Mean time to root cause (MTTR) down by 40% on fallback incidents for onboarded customers.
- For batching helpers: average integration time drop of 25% (self-reported) + fewer retry-related tickets in 30 days.

Open questions and risk flags
- Are we overfitting to the few big customers? Need a quick sampling of smaller self-serve accounts to validate signal.
- Does cost-preview open a new support surface (users expect exact cost and are angry when estimate differs)? We must label as \"estimate\" and show current assumptions.
- Observability costs: adding fallback audit fields to every request may increase log storage; need SRE runbook for retention.

Next steps (practical)
- Nina: spin up 3 stub tickets (one per item above: cost-preview, fallback-audit, batching-helpers) and tag owners. (due: 2026-05-20)
- Diego: prototype SDK cost-preview flag in the JS SDK (alpha) and demo to one beta customer. (due: 2026-05-27)
- Sana: scope log retention impact for fallback audit column with infra and provide cost estimate. (due: 2026-05-25)
- Evan: identify two volunteer accounts for per-route token anomaly pilot. (due: 2026-05-22)

Notes to self / friction snippets to keep in mind:
- Keep messaging humble: \"estimate\" and \"preview\" language matters.
- We should combine small UX changes (humanized retry messages) with backend features to avoid mixed signals.
- Recommend we run a quick 15-min sync with product-observability to align on log schema before any rollout.

If you read one thing: prioritize a tiny cost-preview alpha + one SDK batching helper. They unblock the most common pain signals and are low lift.

Links / references (quick):
- Example ticket cluster: JIRA CS-4011, CS-4042 (cost incidents)
- Customer beta notes: slack thread AB12 (see linked_artifacts)

-- end of harvest diary --

Unresolved: need an air-gapped customer check (who on solutions eng can surface 2 accounts?), and legal sign-off if we add any new telemetry to request logs.
